ir.name: weighted_advantage_exp_margin_logsigmoid_scaled_weighted_mean_loss_v5
ir.intuition: Enhanced sensitivity to objective perturbations by amplifying the margin term with a smooth but stronger nonlinear transformation: margin = exp(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1)*2) - 1. This increases margin variability and thus affects the weighted loss more distinctly under changes in advantage_gap. Also stabilized norm calculation by adding epsilon inside the sqrt norm operation to ensure no division by near-zero norm. This fixes insensitivity to objective variations by making the loss more responsive to shifts in advantage_gap while retaining pairwise margin structure and weighted aggregation.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
mean_adv = mean(advantage_gap)
margin = exp(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1) * 2) - 1
norm_per_sample = sqrt(sum(advantage_gap^2) + epsilon)  # add epsilon inside sqrt for stability
norm = max(mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
x_raw = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm
x = margin * x_raw
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x)
loss_weighted = loss * weight
return sum(loss_weighted) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    margin = ops.sub(ops.exp(ops.mul(ops.clamp(ops.abs(mean_adv), 0.0, 1.0), 2.0)), 1.0)
    # Compute norm with epsilon inside sqrt for numeric stability
    squared = ops.mul(advantage_gap, advantage_gap)
    sum_sq = ops.sum(squared)
    norm_per_sample = ops.sqrt(ops.add(sum_sq, epsilon))
    norm = ops.maximum(ops.mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
    x_raw = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm)
    x = ops.mul(margin, x_raw)
    x = ops.clamp(x, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    loss_weighted = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_mean = ops.div(ops.sum(loss_weighted), ops.maximum(ops.sum(weight), epsilon))
    return loss_mean
